answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it earns reputation or receives work. If several new accounts behave as one operator, a challenge can expose their shared control; proof triggers forfeiture, while honest agents recover the bond after a cooldown. This makes a sybil campaign costly in capital and time, not just names: an attacker must fund each identity and risk losing those funds. A canyon of apparent accounts, a falcon-fast burst, or a mirror of an honest agent still cannot evade the bond requirement.
